tasks.short: Select source documents and reference materials for each data entry assignment.

steps.what: Read the assignment and identify required records in the {ERP}.
Retrieve source documents and reference lists from the {DOCS}.
Check document relevance, versions and completeness before releasing the source pack.

loop.input: Documents whose type or relevance cannot be established from identifiers and metadata.
loop.output: Proposed document matches with source references and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Check assignment identifiers, required document types and versions; the clerk approves the selected pack.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one retry per ambiguous document; unresolved items enter the missing material list.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules handle indexed documents; inconsistent headings and free text require limited interpretation.

tasks.design: Configure assignment requirements in the {ERP}; an integration retrieves matching documents from the {DOCS}. A bounded classifier handles ambiguous documents, and a {WORKFLOW} screen presents the proposed source pack and gaps for clerk approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments, document identifiers and versions were held separately. Manual retrieval was cheaper than maintaining bespoke links.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing metadata and document interfaces support matching. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors and a small review screen.
tasks.still_hard: Missing originals, unreliable version labels and access restrictions still prevent complete packs.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising that a plausible document belongs to the wrong transaction, and finding the responsible document owner.

ambition.what: Check source readiness before each scheduled processing batch.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time retrieving files and more time resolving incomplete assignments. The clerk can return an unready pack with a precise missing material list; transaction approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Improve document indexing for recurring source packs.
reach.learn: Document identifiers, version control and retention categories.

evidence.claim: Identifier matching and completeness rules can assemble recurring source packs without an autonomous agent.
Paperbox organises insurance emails and attachments into case files, supporting document organisation feasibility.

assumptions: The representative setting uses recurring finance or operations assignments with documents in the {DOCS}.
Time shares and remaining effort are design estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Estimates cover one assignment family. GDPR and EU AI Act applicability must be assessed; national rules govern any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Whether assignments contain stable document identifiers.
Whether reference lists and document versions are authoritative.
Which read permissions and interfaces are available.
Whether the proposed work allocation changes require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: How accurately can metadata matching select documents before any model classification is needed?
new_work: Review proposed source packs and unresolved gaps.
Maintain assignment requirements and document matching rules.
Investigate missing documents and broken access links.

tasks.short: Read source documents and enter their values into business records.

steps.what: Read source documents and identify values for the required fields.

loop.input: Residual scanned or free-layout documents after structured imports and fixed-template parsing.
loop.output: Typed field values, source locations and explicit unreadable or missing fields.
loop.check: Validate types, required fields, totals and identifiers; preserve source references and route uncertain values to review.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one retry per document; unresolved fields remain blank and flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured feeds and fixed templates come first; variable layouts and scans need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Key identified values into draft records in the {ERP}.
Compare draft records with source documents and correct errors before acceptance.
Save the accepted batch in the {ERP} and mark the assignment complete.

tasks.design: Import structured source fields directly into draft records in the {ERP}, removing transcription for those inputs. A bounded extractor handles remaining documents from the {DOCS}; configured validation and a source-linked review screen support clerk acceptance before the {ERP} saves the batch.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents varied in layout, and imports lacked consistent mappings or reliable error handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction is available today. AI-assisted coding can shorten mapping, connector and review-screen development.
tasks.still_hard: Poor scans, handwriting, ambiguous identifiers and incorrect originals remain difficult. A matching total does not prove every field is correct.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving conflicting source evidence without inventing values or treating data entry authority as financial approval.

ambition.what: Provide source-linked error reports to teams submitting recurring documents.

tasks.altitude: The clerk reviews highlighted fields and recurring source defects instead of transcribing whole documents. The clerk gains authority to return incomplete submissions, subject to an agreed operating policy.

reach.task: Improve the completeness of incoming document submissions.
reach.learn: Required-field standards and clear correction requests.
Field schemas, duplicate prevention and import error handling.

evidence.claim: Doxis extracts fields from invoices, receipts and attachments.
Rossum documents invoice extraction, validation and ERP integration in the Fugro case.
The proposed effort reduction for mixed data entry documents requires local measurement.

assumptions: The representative batch contains financial or operational records entered into the {ERP}.
Acceptance here confirms transcription accuracy; payment and substantive transaction approvals belong to downstream roles.
Existing imports or extraction configuration are reused before custom development.
Estimates cover one document family and destination. GDPR controls apply; EU AI Act obligations depend on the actual use.
unknowns: Document volumes, languages, scan quality and handwriting frequency.
Whether structured submissions can replace documents at source.
Whether the {ERP} supports draft imports and safe retries.
Which fields require mandatory review and who can accept records.
Data processing permissions and consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: What field-level error and referral rates occur on representative documents, including poor scans?
new_work: Review uncertain values and critical fields.
Maintain mappings, validation rules and representative evaluation samples.
Monitor duplicate imports, rejected records and extraction drift.
Give submitting teams source-linked correction reports.

tasks.short: Record completed batches, activity details and unresolved work in an operational log.

steps.what: Read completion details and batch counts from the {ERP}.
Copy batch identifiers, counts and status into the shared log in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Reconcile logged totals against completed batches and explain discrepancies.

tasks.design: Capture completion events from the {ERP} and configure an append-only activity register in the {WORKFLOW}, replacing the shared {SPREADSHEET}. Deterministic reconciliation compares expected and completed batches; a {BI} view highlights gaps, and the clerk approves discrepancy explanations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completion events were inaccessible or inconsistent across systems. A shared workbook provided a cheap manual bridge.
tasks.enabler_now: Exports and event interfaces can supply the log. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of small connectors and reconciliation views.
tasks.still_hard: Work done outside connected systems can remain invisible. Retries, partial batches and reopened assignments need explicit status rules.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining whether a discrepancy reflects missing work, a system fault or a legitimate processing exception.

ambition.what: Reprioritise unresolved batches each morning using reconciled backlog counts.

tasks.altitude: The clerk stops copying counts and investigates missing or inconsistent events. The clerk can propose the next batch order; the operations supervisor retains staffing and service-priority decisions.

reach.task: Identify recurring delays between document receipt and record acceptance.
reach.learn: Event definitions, reconciliation and process measures.

evidence.claim: Event capture, append-only registers and count reconciliation are deterministic capabilities.
The documented spreadsheet row-limit failure supports checking capacity and completeness in operational logging.
In the Netherlands, worker-monitoring arrangements can require works council consent.

assumptions: A shared workbook bridges the operational system and team reporting in this representative setting.
Existing native logs are assessed before adding a register.
The proposed view measures batches and exceptions; individual productivity monitoring requires separate assessment.
GDPR applies to identifiable activity records. National rules determine employee consultation and monitoring requirements.
unknowns: Whether a native activity register already meets the need.
Which completion events and historical records can be accessed.
Whether current logs support payroll, billing or formal audit evidence.
Retention periods, access roles and applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which reconciliation rules detect missing events without treating retries as additional completed work?
new_work: Investigate missing events and duplicate identifiers.
Maintain status definitions and reconciliation rules.
Approve explanatory corrections while preserving original events.
Review access, retention and reporting changes.

tasks.short: Prepare and load paper or specialist media into office equipment.

steps.what: Read the job ticket in the {DOCS} and identify required media and settings.
Select and load the required media into {OTHER} office equipment.
Inspect the first feed or output sample from {OTHER} office equipment.

tasks.design: Configure media requirements and setup instructions in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to job tickets in the {DOCS}. Use digital delivery where the recipient and process permit it, eliminating those loading jobs; retained physical jobs still require a person to load and inspect {OTHER} office equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loading and checking media require physical handling. Software alone cannot perform those actions.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured job tickets can reduce preparation effort, and digital delivery can remove some jobs. There is no assumed breakthrough in physical loading.
tasks.still_hard: Specialist media, accessibility requirements, jams and first-sample quality checks remain physical work.
tasks.human_edge: Handling unusual media and noticing feed, alignment or tactile defects before a full run.
tasks.altitude: Preparation becomes shorter, but the clerk's physical duties and decision rights largely stay unchanged. Any larger reduction depends on eliminating eligible physical jobs.

reach.task: Assess which recurring output jobs can use digital delivery.
reach.learn: Recipient requirements, accessibility needs and equipment costs.

evidence.claim: Job-ticket configuration can simplify preparation, while physical loading still requires a person.
Digital substitution can eliminate eligible media-handling jobs, subject to recipient and process requirements.

assumptions: Paper is the typical medium; removable or specialist media occur only where the operation requires them.
Step shares describe physical jobs that remain. Possible digital substitution is not counted in their remaining effort.
The estimate covers job-ticket configuration, without equipment replacement.
Access and consultation estimates assume no new worker monitoring; national rules may change the required process.
unknowns: Which equipment and media are actually used.
Which recipients require physical or accessible output.
Whether digital delivery is already available and authorised.
How often loading faults and media changes occur.
research_questions: Which recurring physical jobs can be eliminated while meeting recipient and accessibility requirements?
new_work: Maintain media specifications and setup instructions.
Confirm digital delivery requirements for eligible job types.
Keep equipment fault and media compatibility information current.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward source quality, exception resolution and reliable batch completion. Clerks can gain defined rights to return incomplete submissions and accept verified transcriptions; financial approvals and staffing decisions remain with their existing owners.
reach: File clerk: improve source indexing and version control.
Computer systems analyst: specify field mappings and reliable imports.
Management analyst: investigate recurring processing delays.
Administrative services manager: assess digital substitution for physical output.
skills_to_grow: Clear correction requests and exception escalation.
Basic workflow configuration and access controls.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a shared source-quality service that returns precise correction requests, tracks recurring submission defects and helps adjacent teams prevent them.
